# Kilo CLI native history capture

Pinned writer: `@kilocode/cli@7.8.15` (npm tarball integrity `sha512-vLfP64MSNZkIDrTPY/2GZwWiNnkM0/nDN+mNO6TamAYaGpjnDe2uRnDCdIo4PV/RAO1aevPeBY8vfaaZ0BUdbA==`), macOS arm64, captured 2026-10-22. The binary reports `7.8.15`. This is the current CLI SQLite variant; the older Kilo VS Code extension store was not probed. No provider account, model call, or private history was used.

In an isolated XDG home, `kilo db path` reported `$XDG_DATA_HOME/kilo/kilo.db`. The native `kilo serve` HTTP `POST /session` created an empty session. For reproducible content, `kilo import native-import-before.json` wrote the synthetic user, assistant, and completed tool rows through Kilo's import writer. The writer was exited; a fresh `kilo export ses_kiloTool002` produced `before-resume-official-export.json`. A separate `kilo import native-import-after.json` appended two new messages; another fresh export produced `after-resume-official-export.json`. The SQL fixtures are a deterministic dump of this writer's `project`, `session`, `message`, and `part` rows, omitting unrelated tables. The before fixture omits the appended rows. Native IDs and body JSON are unchanged; paths are synthetic under `/private/tmp/rh-kilo-capture`.

`kilo export` is an independent reader of the database after the writer process exited. It confirms two ordinary turns plus a native `callID`/`tool`/completed `state.output` result, and later resumed turns. It does not prove real model token accounting, native resume control, legacy extension compatibility, or every content part type. Kilo's import writer uses globally unique message/part IDs; a failed import was observed to leave a session row before later validation failed, and attempting a different session with reused message IDs produced an empty exported session. The parser treats each session body independently and retains prior good evidence for malformed bodies.

The SQL files are importable with `sqlite3 target.db < schema-7-8-15.sql`. A separate test derives WAL-only writes and rewritten rows from the same captured schema. SQLite snapshots are read-only and include WAL state; missing databases are not interpreted as deletion unless their configured parent directory remains readable. The Kilo CLI's documented `KILO_DB` override and XDG data directory are resolved once per store. A `:memory:` override has no passive history and reports an unsupported root diagnostic.
